items.title: What Johnson & Johnson (JNJ)'s Bipolar I Mania Data for CAPLYTA Means For Shareholders
items.summary: Johnson & Johnson recently reported positive topline Phase 3 results for CAPLYTA (lumateperone) in adults with bipolar I disorder experiencing manic episodes, showing rapid and statistically significant symptom reduction versus placebo, while also highlighting progress across its broader neuropsychiatry portfolio. The data suggest CAPLYTA could potentially treat both depressive and acute manic episodes in bipolar I disorder, meaningfully broadening its clinical role if future regulatory...

items.title: Could You Have Seen Merck Stock's Pipeline Run Coming?
items.summary: Merck (MRK) stock gained about 89% in the year from mid-September 2025, against a 17.1% price gain for the S&P 500. It also beat Johnson & Johnson (JNJ), up 58%, and Eli Lilly (LLY), up 54%. The signs were public long before the run, in what management kept saying about its drug pipeline. The reported sales told a different story.

items.title: Why Is JNJ Stock Beating Rivals That Grow Faster?
items.summary: Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) stock has returned 58% over the past twelve months, second best in a group of six health care companies. Its revenue growth ranks only fourth of the six. Three peers grew faster and returned less, Eli Lilly among them. The price is a bet that the rest of the business keeps growing once shrinking STELARA sales stop dragging on the total.

items.title: How Far Can BSX Stock Swing After Losing More Than Half Its Value?
items.summary: Boston Scientific (BSX) stock has fallen 55.5% over the past twelve months, and at $43.72 it trades barely above its 52-week low of $42.63. The options market now prices a likely one-year range from $28.46 to $67.16 a share. That band is wide, but it is close to how much the stock has already been moving.

items.title: What Could Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) Gain From Its New Immunology Push?
items.summary: Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ) received FDA approval for ICOTYDE (icotrokinra) to treat moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in the U.S. ICOTYDE targets the IL-23 receptor and is in Phase III clinical trials for a potential psoriatic arthritis indication. The new therapy extends Johnson & Johnson's immunology pipeline beyond oncology and MedTech into chronic inflammatory skin and joint conditions.
